```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.io as pio

# ---- data: facility-level summary built by prepare_data.py ----
fac = pd.read_csv("../data/facilities.csv", dtype={"PROVNUM": str})
fv = fac[fac["hprd"] >= 0.5].copy()          # exclude 20 likely reporting gaps
state = (fv.groupby("STATE")
           .agg(facilities=("PROVNUM", "count"), nurse_hrs=("nurse_hrs", "sum"),
                resident_days=("resident_days", "sum"), contract_hrs=("contract_hrs", "sum"),
                below=("hprd", lambda s: (s < 3).mean()))
           .reset_index())
state["hprd"] = state["nurse_hrs"] / state["resident_days"]
state["contract"] = state["contract_hrs"] / state["nurse_hrs"]

# ---- chart styling (dark slide surface, palette from the dataviz reference) ----
INK, INK2, GRID = "#f0efec", "#c3c2b7", "#383835"
BLUE, RED, GRAY = "#3987e5", "#e66767", "#6b6a64"
base = go.layout.Template(layout=dict(
    paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    font=dict(family="Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif", color=INK2, size=15),
    xaxis=dict(gridcolor=GRID, zerolinecolor=GRID, linecolor=GRID, automargin=True, title_standoff=12),
    yaxis=dict(gridcolor=GRID, zerolinecolor=GRID, linecolor=GRID, automargin=True, title_standoff=12),
    hoverlabel=dict(bgcolor="#262624", bordercolor=GRID, font=dict(color=INK, size=14)),
    margin=dict(l=80, r=20, t=20, b=70)))
pio.templates["deck"] = base
pio.templates.default = "deck"
CONFIG = {"displayModeBar": False, "responsive": True}
from IPython.display import HTML

_js_loaded = False

def show(fig):
    """Render a figure, embedding plotly.js only with the first chart in the deck."""
    global _js_loaded
    html = fig.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs=not _js_loaded, config=CONFIG)
    _js_loaded = True
    return HTML(html)
```

## The short version

::: {.lead}
Staffing is solid on average, but **where** a resident lives matters far more than **how big** their nursing home is.
:::

::: {.incremental}
- **Five states fall below 3.0 hours per resident day**, and in each, roughly 70–80% of facilities do too.
- **Facility size barely predicts care per resident.** Big homes aren't better or worse staffed.
- **Agency staffing ranges from 1.6% to 32% by state**, but it isn't clearly tied to better staffing.
- **361 facilities** had 10+ days below 1.5 hours and belong on a review list.
:::

::: {.footnote}
HPRD = nursing hours (RN + LPN + CNA) ÷ resident days. 3.0 is this analysis's reference line, not a regulation.
:::

## Bigger homes don't give residents more care

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="68%"}
```{python}
p = fv[fv["hprd"] <= 8]
fig = px.scatter(p, x="avg_census", y="hprd", hover_name="PROVNAME",
                 hover_data={"STATE": True, "avg_census": ":.0f", "hprd": ":.2f"},
                 labels={"avg_census": "Average daily residents", "hprd": "Hours per resident day"},
                 opacity=0.35)
fig.update_traces(marker=dict(size=5, color=BLUE, line=dict(width=0)))
fig.add_hline(y=3, line=dict(color=INK2, dash="dash", width=1.5),
              annotation_text="3.0 reference", annotation_font_color=INK2, annotation_position="top right")
fig.update_layout(height=520, width=780)
show(fig)
```
:::
::: {.column width="32%"}
::: {.callout-box}
<span class="big">r = 0.91</span>
census vs. **total** hours. That's just size: big homes employ more nurses.
:::

::: {.callout-box .fragment}
<span class="big accent">r = −0.12</span>
census vs. hours **per resident**. Size tells you almost nothing about care levels.
:::

::: {.small .fragment}
Smallest quarter of homes: **3.52** HPRD. Every other size band: **3.25–3.29**.
:::
:::
:::

## Five states fall below the line, and Texas is the biggest

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="64%"}
```{python}
fig = px.choropleth(state, locations="STATE", locationmode="USA-states", scope="usa",
                    color="hprd", color_continuous_scale=[[0, "#c23b3b"], [0.5, "#383835"], [1, "#3987e5"]],
                    range_color=[2, 4], hover_name="STATE",
                    hover_data={"STATE": False, "hprd": ":.2f", "facilities": True, "below": ":.0%"},
                    labels={"hprd": "HPRD", "facilities": "Facilities", "below": "Below 3.0"})
fig.update_geos(bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", lakecolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", landcolor="#262624",
                subunitcolor="#141413", showlakes=False)
fig.update_layout(height=470, width=800, margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=10, b=10), coloraxis_colorbar=dict(title="HPRD", tickvals=[2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4],
                  ticktext=["≤2.0", "2.5", "3.0", "3.5", "≥4.0"], len=0.7, thickness=12))
show(fig)
```
:::
::: {.column width="36%"}
```{python}
low = state[state["facilities"] >= 10].nsmallest(5, "hprd").sort_values("hprd", ascending=False)
rows = "".join(
    f"<tr><td>{r.STATE}</td><td class='n'>{r.hprd:.2f}</td><td class='n'>{r.below:.0%}</td><td class='n'>{r.facilities:,}</td></tr>"
    for r in low.itertuples())
from IPython.display import HTML
HTML(f"<table class='rank'><thead><tr><th>State</th><th>HPRD</th><th>% below 3.0</th><th>Homes</th></tr></thead><tbody>{rows}</tbody></table>")
```

::: {.small}
**Texas:** 1,167 homes, 77% below 3.0. It was missing from the first draft entirely (see "Three data bugs").

**Highest:** Alaska 5.41, Oregon 4.19, North Dakota 4.08.
:::

## Agency reliance varies 20×, but doesn't buy better staffing

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
```{python}
top = state.sort_values("contract", ascending=True).tail(15)
fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(x=top["contract"], y=top["STATE"], orientation="h",
                       marker=dict(color=[BLUE if s == "VT" else GRAY for s in top["STATE"]],
                                   cornerradius=4),
                       customdata=top[["hprd", "facilities"]],
                       hovertemplate="<b>%{y}</b><br>Contract share: %{x:.1%}<br>HPRD: %{customdata[0]:.2f}<br>Facilities: %{customdata[1]}<extra></extra>"))
fig.update_layout(height=500, width=700, xaxis=dict(tickformat=".0%", title="Share of nursing hours from contract staff"),
                  yaxis=dict(title=""), bargap=0.25)
fig.add_annotation(x=top["contract"].max(), y="VT", text="Vermont 32%", showarrow=False,
                   xanchor="right", xshift=-8, font=dict(color=INK, size=15))
show(fig)
```
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
```{python}
r_state = state["contract"].corr(state["hprd"])
r_fac = fv["contract_share"].corr(fv["hprd"])
fig = px.scatter(state, x="contract", y="hprd", size="facilities", hover_name="STATE",
                 hover_data={"contract": ":.1%", "hprd": ":.2f", "facilities": True},
                 labels={"contract": "Contract share", "hprd": "HPRD"}, size_max=28)
fig.update_traces(marker=dict(color=BLUE, opacity=0.6, line=dict(width=1, color="#141413")))
fig.add_hline(y=3, line=dict(color=INK2, dash="dash", width=1))
fig.update_layout(height=330, width=500, xaxis=dict(tickformat=".0%"), margin=dict(l=60, r=30, t=10, b=60))
fig.add_annotation(x=0.32, y=3.74, text="VT", showarrow=False, yshift=14, font=dict(color=INK, size=13))
show(fig)
```

::: {.small}
Correlation with staffing: **r = `{python} f"{r_state:.2f}"`** across states, **`{python} f"{r_fac:.2f}"`** across facilities. 43.6% of homes use **no** agency staff at all.
:::
:::
:::

## Three data bugs, caught before they reached a decision

::: {.bug-grid}
::: {.bug .fragment}
<span class="tag">Truncation</span>

### Excel silently dropped 21% of the data

The `.xlsx` export stopped at Excel's 1,048,575-row limit. Because the file is sorted by state, **Texas, Vermont, Virginia, Washington and four other states vanished**. Fix: load the source CSV and check counts.
:::

::: {.bug .fragment}
<span class="tag">Identity</span>

### Names aren't IDs

Grouping by facility *name* merged **12 separate "Miller's Merry Manor" homes** into one fake mega-facility. Fix: group by the CMS provider number.
:::

::: {.bug .fragment}
<span class="tag">Missing data</span>

### Zero isn't a staffing level

**20 homes** reported almost no nursing hours all quarter. One averaged 134 residents on 43 hours. Fix: flag as reporting gaps and exclude them.
:::
:::

## Recommendations

::: {.recs}
::: {.rec .fragment}
<span class="n">1</span>
**Focus recruiting on Missouri, Texas, Oklahoma, Indiana and New Mexico.** Their shortfalls are systemic (68–79% of homes below 3.0), not a few outliers.
:::
::: {.rec .fragment}
<span class="n">2</span>
**Verify the 361-facility watchlist** against CMS star ratings and inspections before acting. Some low readings may still be reporting problems.
:::
::: {.rec .fragment}
<span class="n">3</span>
**Review agency spend in Vermont, Maine and New Hampshire.** Converting contract hours to employed staff is a cost question; the data doesn't show it would hurt staffing.
:::
::: {.rec .fragment}
<span class="n">4</span>
**Next analysis:** join star ratings and prior quarters to link staffing to outcomes and track trends.
:::
:::
